purpose: Benztropine is used to treat the symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as muscle stiffness, tremors, and trouble moving. It is also used to treat movement side effects caused by certain psychiatric medications, like antipsychotics. It helps your muscles move more smoothly and comfortably.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called acetylcholine to send signals that control muscle movement. In Parkinson's disease, certain brain chemicals become unbalanced, causing stiffness and shaking. Benztropine works by blocking some of the acetylcholine signals, which helps restore balance and allows your muscles to relax and move more normally.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, blurry vision, constipation, difficulty urinating, drowsiness or dizziness, increased heart rate, and sensitivity to heat. Your mouth may feel very dry, so sipping water and sucking on sugar-free candy can help.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor. Be very careful in hot weather because this drug reduces sweating, which can cause your body to overheat. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, or any trouble urinating, as this medicine may make those conditions worse. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Older adults should use this medication with extra caution because side effects like confusion and dizziness are more common.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 0.5 mg to 1 mg taken by mouth once or twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to 6 mg per day if needed. It can be taken with or without food. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
